title: Neo4jGraph Connect Error
body:
Neo4J Connect error. Note I am able to connect to the DB hosted on neo4j.io

**Neo4j Version:**  5
**Operating System:** Hosted Neo4J Server on neo4j.io / Windows (client)

### Steps to reproduce
from langchain.graphs import Neo4jGraph
from neo4j import GraphDatabase

graph = Neo4jGraph(url=neo4j_boltserver, username=neo4j_username, password=neo4j_password)
# gives error


### Expected behavior
Should Connect

### Actual behavior
We get error: ValueError: Could not connect to Neo4j database. Please ensure that the url is correct

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hi. Thanks for reaching out. Please enable the driver's debug logging and share the output.

```python
from neo4j.debug import watch


watch("neo4j")
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Please double and tripple check your credentials. The logs show that the server rejected them. There's likely a typo, some extraneous whitespace or similar involved.

If going to https://<redacted-host>/?connectURL=neo4j%2Bs%3A%2F%2Fneo4j%<redacted-host> and entering your password works, there's no reason it shouldn't work with the official Python driver (which langchian wraps).

Finally, please note that these kind of questions better are better suited to be asked at the places [I mentioned above](https://github.com/neo4j/neo4j/issues/13255#issuecomment-1681834973).

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Facing this issue, I solved by adding the port at the end of the url.
For example, instead of `neo4j+s://<dbid>.<redacted-host>`, try this `neo4j+s://<dbid>.<redacted-host>:7687`

comments.body: Are you maybe on macOS? I've heard that some installation methods on macOS can lead to Python not having proper access to the system's trusted CAs (certificate authorities). Unfortunately, I can help you much here as I'm not on macOS and don't know much about it either. An internet search might help you resolve the issue.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Please be aware that that instructs the driver to not check the returned certificate's hostname or trust in general. This leaves you vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks. Therefore, I highly recommend to find a permanent solution.
